title: Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Purpose · abstract-1-1】To develop and externally validate a peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics model for predicting early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression after microwave ablation (MWA) and to assess its incremental value over clinical predictors.

evidence.text: To develop and externally validate a peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics model for predicting early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression after microwave ablation (MWA) and to assess its incremental value over clinical predictors.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】This retrospective multicenter study included 376 patients in training (n = 235), internal validation (n = 60), and external validation (n = 81) cohorts. Early progression was defined as local tumor progression or new intrahepatic HCC within 1 year after MWA. Radiomics features were extracted from 5-mm peri-ablational regions on multiphasic CT obtained 1-2 months after MWA. Six machine-learning algorithms and phase combinations were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was combined with independent clinical predictors. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and model interpretability were assessed.

【Results · abstract-3-1】The arterial-plus-portal venous phase (AP + PP) multilayer perceptron model achieved AUCs of 0.857, 0.815, and 0.903 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with performance comparable to the three-phase model. Log10 AFP and tumor size > 2 cm were independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.884, and 0.963, respectively. In external validation, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 84.2%, 96.8%, and 93.8%, respectively. SHAP analysis identified the radiomics score as the most influential predictor.
